svg.text: Why dual contouring: the same sharp corner, two methods
A wedge — the intersection of two half-planes — on an identical grid. Only the vertex-placement rule differs.
Vertices are pinned to grid edges by linear interpolation
of the value, then joined inside each cell. The corner is not
on a grid edge, so no vertex can ever be placed there.
Refining shrinks the chord — it never removes it.
One vertex per cell, placed anywhere inside it by minimising
the squared distance to the planes the Hermite normals define.
The corner cell has two independent normals, so the two plane
constraints intersect at exactly one point: the corner.
